The '''Dagadusheth Halwai Ganapati Temple''' is a [[Hindu temple]] dedicated to the Hindu god [[Ganesha]] (Ganapati) in the city of [[Pune]], India. The temple is visited by over one hundred thousand devotees every year.<ref>{{cite book|last=Zelliot|first=Eleanor|author2=Maxine Berntsen|title=The Experience of Hinduism: Essays on Religion in Maharashtra|publisher=SUNY Press|year=1988|page=[https://archive.org/details/experienceofhind00zell/page/104 104]|isbn=978-0-88706-664-1|url=https://archive.org/details/experienceofhind00zell/page/104}}</ref> A large number of devotees visit the temple during the annual ten-day public ''[[Ganesh Chaturthi|Ganeshotsav]]'' festival.<ref name="Deccan" /> The main Ganesha idol is insured for a sum of {{INRConvert|10|m}}.<ref name="Ganesh clears obstacles for women reciting Atharvasheersha">{{cite news |url=http://www.hindustantimes.in/StoryPage/StoryPage.aspx?sectionName=&id=35602b5f-00d8-40dd-b95a-d962c077bc90&&Headline=Ganesh+clears+obstacles+for+women+reciting+EMAtharvasheersha%2fEM |title=Ganesh clears obstacles for women reciting Atharvasheersha |date=4 September 2008 |work=Hindustan Times |access-date=5 December 2008 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120531193606/http://www.hindustantimes.in/StoryPage/StoryPage.aspx?sectionName=&id=35602b5f-00d8-40dd-b95a-d962c077bc90&&Headline=Ganesh+clears+obstacles+for+women+reciting+EMAtharvasheersha%2FEM |archive-date=31 May 2012 |df=dmy }}</ref> It celebrated 132 years of its ''Ganeshotsav'' festival in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dagdusheth Ganpati|url=https://www.dagdushethganpati.com/|url-status=live|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20021125060208/http://dagdushethganpati.com:80/ |archive-date=25 November 2002 }}</ref>

== History ==
Dagadusheth Halwai was a successful sweet seller (Halwai) and a rich businessman in the city of Pune in the late 1800s. His original halwai shop still exists under the name "Dagdusheth Halwai Sweets" near Datta Mandir in Pune. In the late 1800s, he and his wife Laxmibai lost their only son in a [[Bubonic plague|plague]] epidemic. The grieving couple followed the advice of a sage  to build a Ganesh temple in Pune in his memory.<ref name="TOI">{{cite news |last= Sengar|first= Resham|date=4 September 2019|title=125 years ago, a halwai made this famous Ganpati temple in Pune|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/travel/destinations/125-years-ago-a-halwai-made-this-famous-ganpati-temple-in-pune/articleshow/70979655.cms|newspaper=Times of India| access-date= 31 October 2022}}</ref>
Later, Dagdusheth adopted, his nephew Govindsheth (born 1865) who was 9 years old at the time of his death. Govindsheth replaced the first Ganesh idol by a new one, with the first one still being present at Akra Maruti Chowk. A generous man, he established an additional  Ganesh idol in a wrestling gym called Jagoba Dada Talim. This talim was owned by Dagdusheth as he was also a former wrestling trainer. One of the chowk (square) in Pune is named Govind Halwai Chowk, after him. Along with his mother, Govindsheth handled all the programmes like Ganesh Utsav, Datta Jayanti and other festivities. The residence where they resided is now known as Laxmibai Dagdusheth Halwai Sansthan Datta Mandir Trust. Laxmi Road in Pune is named after Laxmibai Dagdusheth halwai.{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}} Govindsheth died in 1943. His son Dattatray Govindsheth Halwai, born in 1926, was the one who established the third Ganesh idol replacing the second.This idol, known as Navasacha Ganpati, is the one that is present today in the Dagdusheth temple. It proved to be an epoch-making event in Indian history.{{According to whom|date=March 2025}}<ref name="IE">{{cite news |last= Rashid|first= Atikh|date=4 September 2022|title=Know Your City: Dagadusheth Halwai, the wrestler-trader behind Pune's most popular Ganpati temple|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/pune/pune-know-your-city-dagadusheth-halwai-ganpati-temple-8128585/|newspaper=Indian Express| access-date= 31 October 2022}}</ref>

The temples's [[Ganeshotsav]] [[pandal]] was not put up for the first time in 128 years, in 2020 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name=Pandal>{{cite news |last=Pandit |first=Shiladitya |date=11 August 2020 |title=First time in 128 years, Dagdusheth mandal lets go of pandal over Covid |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/first-time-in-128-years-dagdusheth-mandal-lets-go-of-pandal-over-covid/articleshow/77471849.cms |work=The Times of India |location=Pune |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250304164031/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/first-time-in-128-years-dagdusheth-mandal-lets-go-of-pandal-over-covid/articleshow/77471849.cms |archive-date=4 March 2025 |access-date=4 March 2025}}</ref>

==Temple==
[[File:Dagdusheth Ganpati, Pune.jpeg|left|thumb|The central icon of Ganesha]]
The temple is over 100 years old. Jay and Vijay, the two sentinels made of marble catch the eye of all at the outset. The construction is so simple that all the proceedings in the temple along with the Ganesh idol can be seen even from outside. The Ganesh idol is  2.2 metres tall and 1 metre wide. It is adorned with nearly 40 kilos of gold. The temple conducts  Daily pooja, abhisheka and the arti of the Ganesh. The temple is illuminated during the Ganesh festival. Shrimant Dagdusheth Ganpati Trust manages the temple. The temple is situated in the centre of city, local shopping market is also the nearby temple. Various cultural activities like music concerts, bhajans, and Atharvasheersh recitation are organized by the trust.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shrimant Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati Mandir in Pune|url=http://www.punesite.com/shrimant-dagdusheth-halwai-ganpati-mandir-in-pune.html|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190114210641/http://www.punesite.com/shrimant-dagdusheth-halwai-ganpati-mandir-in-pune.html|archive-date=14 January 2019|website=www.punesite.com}}</ref>
He later established the Halwai Ganapati Trust.<ref name="Rediff">{{cite news|url=http://www.rediff.com/news/sep/04pune.htm|title=Pune's Dagedu Sheth Halwai dresses up for Ganeshotsva|last=Zore|first=Prasanna D|year=1997|work=Rediff|access-date=4 December 2008}}</ref><ref name="Deccan">{{cite news|url=http://www.deccanherald.com/Content/Sep92007/sundayherald2007090623817.asp |title=Pune leads the community |last=Rabade |first=Parag |date=9 July 2007 |work=Deccan Herald |access-date=4 December 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081121004839/http://www.deccanherald.com/Content/Sep92007/sundayherald2007090623817.asp |archive-date=21 November 2008 }}</ref> [[Bal Gangadhar Tilak]], during the [[British Raj]], gave a public form to the Ganesh festival celebrations as a way of getting around an order that barred public meetings.<ref name="Rediff" />
Shri Datta Mandir in Budhwar Peth, Pune was the residence of the Halwai family. In Pune, Govind Halwai has a chowk (square) named after him.

A replica of the temple was built in [[Phuket]], Thailand.<ref name=Phuket>{{cite news |last=Jhangiani |first=Anjali |date=31 October 2024 |title=A slice of Pune now in Phuket: Thai replica of iconic Dagdusheth Temple |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/dutch-ganesha-in-thailand-replica-of-punes-dagdusheth-temple-unveiled-in-phuket/articleshow/114790435.cms |work=[[The Times of India]]|location=[[Pune]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241031165454/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/dutch-ganesha-in-thailand-replica-of-punes-dagdusheth-temple-unveiled-in-phuket/articleshow/114790435.cms |archive-date=31 October 2024 |access-date=4 March 2025}}</ref>

== Temple Trust ==
The Shrimant Dagadusheth Halwai Ganapati Trust carries out philanthropic work from the donations received, and is one of the richest in Maharashtra.<ref name="TOI1">{{cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshow/1625198.cms|title=Topper has 'mandal' effect to thank for|last=Damle|first=Manjiri|date=6 July 2006|work=Times of India|access-date=4 December 2008}}</ref> The trust operates an [[old age home]] called ''Pitashree'' at Kondhwa in Pune. The home was opened in May 2003.<ref name="CM to inaugurate charitable old-age home on Sunday.">{{cite news|date=24 May 2003|title=CM to inaugurate charitable old-age home on Sunday.|work=Times of India|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/cm-to-inaugurate-charitable-old-age-home-on-sunday/articleshow/47204940.cms|access-date=4 December 2008}}</ref> In the same building the trust provides housing and education for 400 destitute children.<ref name="TOI1" /> Other services provided by the trust include ambulance service for poor and health clinics in tribal belts of [[Pune District]].<ref name="Social activities">{{cite web|url=http://www.dagadushethganapati.com/trustee/activities.htm|title=Social activities|publisher=Dagadusheth Ganapati Trust|access-date=4 December 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100405192143/http://www.dagadushethganapati.com/trustee/activities.htm|archive-date=5 April 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[Ganesh festival]], [[Gudhi Padwa]] till [[Ram Navami]] are the festivals celebrated by Dagadusheth halwai Ganapati Trust, Pune.{{citation needed|date=July 2021}}
